audit.why: 46.74% over 1853 games — the hardest lane in this slice. Levels 1-3 are a free poke window against a champion with no shield and no gap-closer; from Soul Furnace onward it is his lane and it never comes back.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart reads Jayce|Skill|Sion|Sion|Jayce|Sion|Sion, but whys[2] calls level 3 'your hardest-favor window' and whys[4] says level 6 'flips to him'. The chart gives Sion level 3 and Jayce level 6 — both backwards.
audit.why: early states 'Levels 1-3 are your whole window'. Packet reference chart Jayce|Jayce|Jayce|Sion|Sion|Sion|Sion is what the page actually argues.
audit.corrected: Sides re-set to Jayce, Jayce, Jayce, Sion, Sion, Sion, Sion.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says the gate-Q 'out-ranges all of his tools' and that he has nothing to answer with. Roar of the Slayer (E) is exactly that answer: Riot's text says if the shockwave hits a minion it KNOCKS THE MINION BACK, damaging, slowing and REDUCING THE ARMOR of everything it passes through. Also Glory in Death (P) heals him on every attack in the zombie state and the page never mentions healing at all.
audit.why: The minion-punt is how a Sion trades back into a ranged poke lane from outside his own 600-ish reach, and eating the armour shred is what turns his follow-up into real damage. And a passive that heals decides whether the post-death fight goes your way — Grievous Wounds timing is a real decision the page skips.
audit.corrected: Roar of the Slayer's minion knockback stated in early, mid and whys[3]; Glory in Death's healing and the Grievous Wounds call added to the late spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flagged defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere.
audit.why: Decimating Smash 10/9/8/7/6s, Soul Furnace 15/14/13/12/11s, Roar of the Slayer 12/11/10/9/8s, Unstoppable Onslaught 140/100/60s. Soul Furnace's 15s at rank 1 is the shield window that decides whether your orb lands for value.
audit.corrected: 15s W stated in mid and whys[3].

edits.before: This is where it slips. Once Sion finishes a tank item and Soul Furnace is online, he pops the W shield to eat your gate-Q on demand, and your poke — the entire reason you win lane — stops mattering. He farms through it with his autos and zombie passive, so you can't zone or deny him the way you bully a melee bruiser. At 6 his Unstoppable Onslaught is a real lane-spanning engage knockup while your R is only the stance swap, so respect his all-in and never get caught walking up in Hammer form with his Q charged.
edits.after: This is where it slips. Once Sion finishes a tank item and Soul Furnace is online he pops the 15s W shield to eat your gate-Q on demand, and your poke — the entire reason you win lane — stops mattering. He answers back with Roar of the Slayer: hit a minion with it and the minion is punted through you, slowing you and shredding your armor from outside his own reach. At 6 Unstoppable Onslaught is a lane-spanning engage knockup while your R is only the stance swap, so never walk up in Hammer form with his Q charged.

edits.before: Soul Furnace comes online and Sion pops the W shield to eat your gate-Q on demand, neutralizing the poke war while he farms safely through it.
edits.after: Soul Furnace comes online: a 15s W shield eats your gate-Q on demand, and Roar of the Slayer punts a minion back through you for a slow and armor shred.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are your whole window, so abuse them: take Cannon Q, drop Acceleration Gate, and fire Shock Blast through it at every step-up Sion makes to last-hit. The accelerated gate-Q out-ranges all of his tools and the Cannon-to-Hammer swap shreds his Armor and MR for a free chunk. He has no Soul Furnace shield yet and no gap-closer to answer you, so build a health lead and pressure plates. The one thing to respect is a fully charged Decimating Smash; if he winds it up, you can interrupt it with Hammer-form Thundering Blow before the knockup channels, but mostly just sidestep it and keep poking.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are your whole window, so abuse them: take Cannon Q, drop Acceleration Gate, and fire Shock Blast through it at every step-up Sion makes to last-hit. The accelerated gate-Q out-ranges his walk-up and the Cannon-to-Hammer swap shreds his Armor and MR for a free chunk. He has no Soul Furnace shield yet, so build a health lead and pressure plates — but his reach is Roar of the Slayer punting a minion back through you for a slow and armor shred. The other thing to respect is a fully charged Decimating Smash; if he winds it up, sidestep it and keep poking.

edits.before: By two items the tank scaling flips the lane: a fully charged Decimating Smash (Q) knockup plus Onslaught locks down your squishy frame long enough that he doesn't need to out-damage you. You can't 1v1 him, so split and end on the map.
edits.after: By two items a charged Decimating Smash (Q) knockup into Onslaught locks your squishy frame long enough that he need not out-damage you, and Glory in Death heals him off every zombie auto — Grievous Wounds decides that fight. Split and end on the map.

notes: Unstoppable Onslaught: the page tells you to hold Thundering Blow for his engage. Whether the knockback actually stops the R charge is not answerable from Riot's text or the kit file (needsResearch is empty), so I did NOT put any claim about it on the page. Flagged in unverified — this one is worth a human answer because the whole level-6 advice hangs on it. Roar of the Slayer's minion-punt was completely absent and is how Sion trades back into ranged poke.
